lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Good morning. It's four a.m. Right now, you're asleep. That's why you're broke. I've been up since three. I've already had a cold shower, a hot shower, and an argument with a swan.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Somewhere right now, a man is standing next to a very clean car, telling you to wake up at four in the morning so you can be rich like him.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And if you watch to the end, he'll tell you exactly how he made his money.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It was selling you this video.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I'm still watching.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So. Is hustle culture a scam?

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Hustle culture is the belief that success comes from working all the time, sleeping as little as possible, and turning every hobby you enjoy into a business you don't.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Its best customers are people who are already exhausted, being told the problem is that they aren't exhausted enough.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Rise and grind.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: He has a slogan for waking up. Most people just make a noise.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And it isn't just guys with ring lights. In 2019, Alibaba's founder Jack Ma called China's nine-nine-six schedule a huge blessing. Nine a.m. to nine p.m., six days a week.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I wanted to know what that looks like from the inside. So I asked Gerald.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Hi, Ryan. I'm Gerald, from People and Culture. Nobody's in trouble. I just want to talk. Let's start small. Saturday. You don't need all of Saturday. Do you?

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I... sort of use it.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Of course. And that's completely valid. What if you kept the morning, and we just quietly looked after the afternoon for you?

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Put the weekend down, Ryan. Slowly. Nobody has to get hurt.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Good news, though. You can get it back. We've moved weekends to a subscription model. Weekend Lite gives you Saturday morning, with occasional emails. Weekend Plus adds Sunday, but the Sunday evening dread is billed separately. And Weekend Pro includes the afternoon you just gave me.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I just gave you that.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: And now you can have it back. Monthly.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Can I just... have the one I had before?

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: That plan's been discontinued. But we've kept your memories of it in a premium folder.

lines.speaker: inner
lines.text: He's good.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: And if you'd rather sleep when you're dead, we've partnered with a lovely cemetery. Staff get ten percent off.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: How do I cancel?

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Cancellations are done in person. On a Saturday.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Then there's the sacred early morning. Robin Sharma's 2018 book The 5 AM Club sold millions of copies telling people to get up before the sun.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: I tried it, actually. Day one, I did yoga. Day two, I journaled. On day three, I woke up at five, looked at the ceiling, and said no out loud. To nobody.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It's the most honest I've ever been.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Four a.m., awake. Four oh five, ice bath. Four thirty, I read one page of a book about reading. Five, I tell the mirror it's a winner.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Six, I film my morning routine. Seven, I edit my morning routine. Nine, I post my morning routine.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So the main thing his morning produces is a video of his morning.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: I tried it once. Got up at four, cold shower, and by six I'd done everything I needed to do that day. Then I realised everyone I needed was asleep. So I just sat in my kitchen. Fully dressed. Like a butler with no house.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Effort does matter, to be fair. The famous ten thousand hour rule comes from the psychologist Anders Ericsson's research on experts, although he said there was nothing magic about the number.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Ten thousand hours. That's...

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: No, I had something for this.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It's gone. I got up at five.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Side hustles are real. In 2025, Bankrate found about twenty-seven percent of American adults had one. For plenty of them, it's how the rent gets paid.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The average side hustle earns eight hundred and eighty-five dollars a month.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The median, the person exactly in the middle, earns two hundred.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The average is a liar standing next to a millionaire.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Then there's multi-level marketing, where you sell products and recruit your friends to sell them too.

lines.speaker: inner
lines.text: Text your ex. Sell her a candle.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: No.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In 2018, an AARP Foundation survey of people who'd joined one found forty-seven percent lost money. Twenty-seven percent broke even.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: So a quarter of them did unpaid work.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Enthusiastically.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And all those extra hours have to come from somewhere. For Brayden, they come out of the night. Which, unfortunately, his body was using.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Team. Let's talk about sleep. Every night, eight hours, gone. No revenue. No content. I'm not paying you to lie there in the dark.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Heart. Love the energy. You're getting more responsibility.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Liver, I've seen your numbers. You're on a performance plan.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Kidneys. Two of you, doing the same job. That's a redundancy situation.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: He fired a kidney.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Sorry. The actual science. In 2000, Australian researchers found that after seventeen to nineteen hours awake, people did some tests as badly as someone with a blood alcohol level of zero point zero five percent.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So a man who got up at four is, by ten p.m., cognitively two glasses of wine into a wedding. Except nobody's dancing, and he's trying to sell you a webinar.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Sleep is a mindset.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: It isn't. Researchers think one of the things sleep does is clear waste out of the brain. Skip it, and you're running the whole operation on yesterday's rubbish.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Where do you think you're going?

lines.speaker: inner
lines.text: Breathwork. Ninety-nine dollars.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Absolutely not.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: More hours don't even mean more work. The Stanford economist John Pencavel studied British munitions workers in the First World War. Their output at seventy hours a week was barely different from their output at fifty-six.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Those extra fourteen hours produced nothing. They were just looking busy. A craft that workers have since refined into the little green available dot next to their name.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And sometimes it isn't funny at all. In 2021, the World Health Organization and the International Labour Organization estimated that long working hours led to seven hundred and forty-five thousand deaths from stroke and heart disease in 2016.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So why does any of this feel true?

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: This is the hustle success story. And this...

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: ...is everyone else.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Ryan?

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: It was a lockdown thing.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: In the Second World War, the statistician Abraham Wald was shown bombers covered in bullet holes, and asked where to add armour. He pointed out that the planes hit everywhere else never came back to be counted.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: If hustle gurus had been in charge, they'd have armoured the bullet holes and called it a mindset.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: You only ever hear from the guy on top. Nobody hosts a podcast called How I Lost Everything Selling Phone Cases.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Although honestly, I'd listen.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And where there's a dream, there's a course. In 2024, the US Federal Trade Commission went after schemes selling passive income from AI-powered online stores. Customers paid tens of thousands of dollars. For nearly all of them, the FTC said, the money never arrived.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: You know you've made it when the government knows your name.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: People are pushing back. In 2021, a post about lying flat went viral in China. Doing the absolute minimum, on purpose.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: And in 2019, Microsoft Japan closed its offices every Friday in August. Sales per employee went up almost forty percent.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So, wellness.

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: We hear you. So we've installed a beanbag, and booked a one-hour webinar on resilience. It's during your lunch break.

lines.speaker: benny
lines.text: Is the beanbag mandatory?

lines.speaker: gerald
lines.text: Of course not. It's optional. Like the weekend.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: So is hustle culture a scam? Not the work. Work is real, and some people genuinely love building things at midnight. Good for them.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: The scam is the packaging. Exhaustion sold as a personality, survivors sold as proof, and your insecurity sold back to you at a monthly rate.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Link in bio.

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Oh, and Brayden's four a.m. videos?

lines.speaker: maya
lines.text: Filmed at four in the afternoon. The sunrise is a lamp.

lines.speaker: brayden
lines.text: Still counts.
